title: Factor topology and node-function Views for graph programs
hypothesis: Factoring graph topology from node-function identity lets a shared graph substrate compose unseen topology×function roles at lower complete bytes and active work than independent program networks and ordinary modular routing.

world.teacher: shared node-function basis and topology-specific sparse connectivity; heldout pairings combine stored topology and function codes

fresh.release_rule: Keep fresh sealed after native modular-routing alias or storage/quality gate miss.

controls: shared graph substrate with native topology IDs and function IDs
fixed topology and fixed node function
metrics: full serialized inference bytes including graph/function metadata
success_gate: heldout nRMSE <=0.02, >=25% fewer full bytes than independent, and strict quality/compute improvement over native modular routing.
failure_gate: FAIL if native module/topology IDs implement the same composition or gates miss.
boundaries: Synthetic linear graph programs only; no Neural Interpreter or GrapNet reproduction.
Heldout pair IDs and constituent topology/function codes are present in payload; this tests compositional decoding, not unseen-code inference.
No fresh runs after native alias or gate miss.
